manifest.title: Ω System Ontology — Totality and World-Inscription Graph
manifest.description: Graph-native ontology revised around the One-System principle: Totality is the sole physically continuous system; local systems are effective individuations within it. The update adds causal coherence, trace lineages, direct and relayed inscription, cross-carrier convergence, and world-grounded learned regions.
scope: Totality as the single physically continuous causal system
local systems as analytic or dynamically effective cuts within Totality
constraint-shaped causal possibility and receiver-relative differential effects
formal, inscribed, executing, natural, and hybrid systems
exact anchors, exact basins, and reconstructible regions
causal coherence, causal traces, and feature preservation
direct, adaptive, relayed, and aggregated inscription
cross-carrier convergence and world-grounded learned regions
history, conditioning, plasticity, and token-by-token path realization
semantic-feature communication through a graph-native ontology

nodes.label: Ω System Ontology
nodes.definition: A graph ontology for communicating the semantic feature set of Totality: constraint-shaped causal possibility, receiver-relative effects, state persistence, world-grounded inscription, and the convergence of natural, formal, and hybrid systems.

nodes.label: Local system
nodes.definition: An effectively individuated region of Totality with a repertoire of states and relations. Its boundary is analytically or dynamically useful, not an ontological separation from Totality.

nodes.label: Receiver system
nodes.definition: A local system whose organization makes some perturbations differentially consequential for its future trajectories.

nodes.label: Natural dynamic system
nodes.definition: A physically instantiated local region of Totality whose organization and state are sustained through ongoing dynamics.

nodes.label: Formal structure
nodes.definition: An abstract specification of admissible states, relations, or transformations.

nodes.label: Inscribed structure
nodes.definition: A physically persistent encoding of formal, learned, or historical structure.

nodes.label: Executing process
nodes.definition: An energy-dependent physical realization that applies transitions and occupies changing states.

nodes.label: Hybrid system
nodes.definition: A local region of Totality in which durable inscription and dynamic execution jointly produce complex, history-sensitive behavior.

nodes.label: Environment
nodes.definition: The region of Totality treated as external relative to a selected local system boundary, including the systems and conditions with which that region exchanges matter, energy, or constraints.

nodes.label: Subsystem
nodes.definition: A local system individuated as a constituent region within another local system cut.

nodes.label: Continuous process
nodes.definition: An executing process whose organization persists through ongoing activity.

nodes.label: Episodic process
nodes.definition: An executing process instantiated in bounded episodes and absent between them as that particular active process.

nodes.label: Object–process continuum
nodes.definition: A spectrum describing systems by the relative contribution of passive persistence, durable inscription, and actively maintained dynamics.

nodes.label: State
nodes.definition: A configuration of a system at a specified level of description.

nodes.label: State space
nodes.definition: The set or structured space of states available in a system description.

nodes.label: Accessible state region
nodes.definition: The portion of state space reachable under current constraints and conditions.

nodes.label: Realized state
nodes.definition: The state actually occupied at a given step or interval.

nodes.label: State persistence
nodes.definition: The preservation, maintenance, or reconstructibility of a state or state-relevant structure across time.

nodes.label: Passive persistence
nodes.definition: State persistence produced by resistance to change without active refresh.

nodes.label: Inscribed persistence
nodes.definition: State persistence produced by a durable physical encoding.

nodes.label: Active persistence
nodes.definition: State persistence requiring ongoing energy-dependent maintenance or refresh.

nodes.label: Recursive persistence
nodes.definition: Active persistence in which maintained organization contributes to maintaining the conditions of its own continuation.

nodes.label: Plastic persistence
nodes.definition: Persistence that retains changes affecting later transition tendencies.

nodes.label: Reconstructive persistence
nodes.definition: Continuity achieved by re-instantiating an appropriate state from preserved external structure rather than maintaining the original active process.

nodes.label: Continuity mechanism
nodes.definition: The physical or procedural means by which state persistence is realized.

nodes.label: Checkpoint
nodes.definition: A preserved record sufficient to support later reconstruction of selected state structure.

nodes.label: Reinstantiation
nodes.definition: Creation of a new executing process from preserved inscription and, where available, a checkpoint.

nodes.label: Resumption
nodes.definition: Continuation of the same executing process from a preserved active execution state.

nodes.label: Constraint
nodes.definition: A condition that restricts, weights, enables, or suppresses states and transitions.

nodes.label: Structural constraint
nodes.definition: A constraint arising from durable organization or topology.

nodes.label: Dynamic constraint
nodes.definition: A constraint arising from current activity, gradients, or transient state.

nodes.label: Context constraint
nodes.definition: A constraint supplied by the currently accumulated local context.

nodes.label: Historical constraint
nodes.definition: A constraint produced by prior trajectories, learning, or inherited structure.

nodes.label: Rule constraint
nodes.definition: An explicit operation or selection rule applied to a state transition.

nodes.label: Effective transition topology
nodes.definition: The currently operative pattern of permitted, suppressed, and weighted transitions among states.

nodes.label: Transition
nodes.definition: A change from one state to another.

nodes.label: Selection
nodes.definition: Realization of one continuation from the currently available continuation field.

nodes.label: Unique-successor map
nodes.definition: A transition specification assigning exactly one successor or terminal result to each declared state.

nodes.label: Distributional transition field
nodes.definition: A transition specification assigning a probability distribution or weighted set of successors to a state.

nodes.label: Exact execution specification
nodes.definition: A complete operational description sufficient to resolve a distributional or underspecified process into a repeatable realized path.

nodes.label: Continuation field
nodes.definition: The locally generated weighted set of immediate continuations available from an instantiated state.

nodes.label: Latent continuation space
nodes.definition: The structured set of possible future trajectories reachable from a state under the operative transition topology.

nodes.label: Continuation tree
nodes.definition: A path-unfolded representation of possible future histories, duplicating reconvergent states when reached by different paths.

nodes.label: Future cone
nodes.definition: The subset or measure of continuations compatible with a realized history prefix.

nodes.label: Trajectory
nodes.definition: An ordered sequence of realized or possible transitions.

nodes.label: Realized path
nodes.definition: The particular trajectory actually taken.

nodes.label: Recurrence
nodes.definition: Return to a previously occupied state or recurrent structure under continued transition.

nodes.label: Terminal halt
nodes.definition: A terminal condition with no successor under a declared transition specification.

nodes.label: Exact anchor
nodes.definition: A precisely defined terminal halt or recurrent structure that organizes exact path convergence.

nodes.label: Exact basin
nodes.definition: Under a unique-successor map, the set of states sharing the same exact anchor.

nodes.label: Reconstructible region
nodes.definition: A stable but potentially graded region repeatedly reachable through a bounded family of constraints and approach paths, whose structure is grounded in causal history and changes later transitions.

nodes.label: Approach space
nodes.definition: The collection of trajectories or constraint sequences capable of reaching a region or anchor.

nodes.label: Attractor-like structure
nodes.definition: A region or tendency toward which multiple trajectories converge without requiring exact terminal equivalence.

nodes.label: Repeller-like structure
nodes.definition: A region or tendency from which trajectories are systematically redirected or excluded.

nodes.label: Neighborhood
nodes.definition: A set of nearby or relationally adjacent states or regions under a declared topology or metric.

nodes.label: Perturbation
nodes.definition: A physical or formal difference introduced to a system.

nodes.label: Patterned perturbation
nodes.definition: A perturbation whose relational or temporal organization is available to receiver sensitivity.

nodes.label: Coupling event
nodes.definition: An interaction in which a perturbation and a receiver jointly participate in a state change.

nodes.label: Receiver sensitivity
nodes.definition: Receiver organization that makes a class of perturbations capable of producing differential downstream effects.

nodes.label: Receiver insensitivity
nodes.definition: Receiver organization that suppresses or absorbs a class of perturbations without the target differential effect.

nodes.label: Threshold
nodes.definition: A boundary at which a perturbation changes the accessible transition regime.

nodes.label: Metastable state
nodes.definition: A temporarily persistent state maintained away from equilibrium and susceptible to selected transitions.

nodes.label: Far-from-equilibrium gradient
nodes.definition: Available energetic displacement supporting maintained organization and receiver-supplied causal work.

nodes.label: Energy transfer
nodes.definition: Physical energy exchanged during a coupling event.

nodes.label: Receiver-supplied energy
nodes.definition: Energy already available within or to the receiver and mobilized in the downstream response.

nodes.label: Amplification
nodes.definition: Production of a downstream effect whose energetic scale exceeds the triggering perturbation by drawing on receiver-supplied energy.

nodes.label: Causal cascade
nodes.definition: A chained sequence of transitions initiated or redirected by a coupling event.

nodes.label: Counterfactual baseline
nodes.definition: The receiver trajectories expected under a specified alternative in which the target coupling or perturbation differs or is absent.

nodes.label: Trajectory delta
nodes.definition: The structured difference between downstream accessible or weighted trajectories under a coupling and its counterfactual baseline.

nodes.label: Ω-event
nodes.definition: A receiver-relative coupling that produces a non-null trajectory delta because the receiver maps the perturbation into a different downstream continuation.

nodes.label: Causal surface
nodes.definition: A coarse-grained pattern that is available for coupling at a receiver-relevant scale while underlying detail remains causally constitutive but locally opaque.

nodes.label: Coherent pattern
nodes.definition: A pattern whose constituent outcomes preserve a stable relational feature across events or scales and jointly support a receiver-relevant distinction.

nodes.label: History
nodes.definition: The realized sequence of prior states, transitions, and couplings relevant to current organization.

nodes.label: Path dependence
nodes.definition: Dependence of current accessibility or weighting on the trajectory by which the current state was reached.

nodes.label: Conditioning
nodes.definition: Temporary alteration of current continuation fields by accumulated state or context without necessarily changing durable inscription.

nodes.label: Inscription change
nodes.definition: A persistent alteration to inscribed structure that changes future transition generation.

nodes.label: Plasticity
nodes.definition: Capacity for realized activity to produce inscription change.

nodes.label: Training
nodes.definition: A procedure that alters durable transition-generating structure through selected examples, objectives, or feedback.

nodes.label: Development
nodes.definition: History-dependent formation and reorganization of a system during its lifetime.

nodes.label: Evolutionary selection
nodes.definition: Differential persistence and reproduction that inscribes receiver organization across lineages.

nodes.label: Token
nodes.definition: A discrete symbol available as an input, output, or state-bearing element in a sequential process.

nodes.label: Token event
nodes.definition: Selection or admission of a token that extends realized history and conditions subsequent continuations.

nodes.label: Context update
nodes.definition: A change in current context caused by incorporating a realized event or token.

nodes.label: Scale
nodes.definition: A declared level of spatial, temporal, organizational, or descriptive resolution.

nodes.label: Microstate
nodes.definition: A state description at a finer-grained scale.

nodes.label: Macro-pattern
nodes.definition: A coarser pattern constituted by regularities across finer-grained states or interactions.

nodes.label: Coarse-graining
nodes.definition: Projection from fine-grained detail to a lower-dimensional pattern or distinction.

nodes.label: Projection
nodes.definition: A mapping that preserves selected structure while discarding other detail.

nodes.label: Cross-scale coupling
nodes.definition: A coupling in which patterns at one scale alter accessible trajectories at another scale through the same physical system.

nodes.label: Shared fate
nodes.definition: Persistent coordination of constituent trajectories sufficient to support treatment as one system.

nodes.label: Isolability
nodes.definition: The degree to which a system can be separated or relocated while preserving its relevant organization and membership.

nodes.label: Receiver-relative causal repertoire
nodes.definition: A receiver’s organization determines which perturbations become consequential and what downstream continuations they make available.

nodes.label: Constraint-shaped transition topology
nodes.definition: Constraints carve an effective transition topology from a larger possibility space by permitting, suppressing, and weighting transitions.

nodes.label: Ω-event criterion
nodes.definition: A coupling qualifies as an Ω-event when it produces a non-null trajectory delta relative to an explicit counterfactual baseline.

nodes.label: Receiver-side amplification
nodes.definition: A perturbation may redirect a much larger causal process because amplification draws on receiver-supplied energy rather than requiring the perturbation to supply the full downstream energy.

nodes.label: History conditions futures
nodes.definition: Realized history changes the continuation field from which later trajectories are selected.

nodes.label: Plasticity reshapes the generator
nodes.definition: When history produces inscription change, it alters the durable structure that generates future continuation fields.

nodes.label: Exact basin boundary
nodes.definition: Exact basins require a declared unique-successor map and exact anchor; the term must not be silently generalized to all stable semantic or dynamic regions.

nodes.label: Reconstructible-region realism
nodes.definition: A graded region may be treated as operationally real when actual causal histories helped inscribe it, bounded constraints and approach paths repeatedly reconstruct characteristic structure, and its activation changes later transitions.

nodes.label: Two approaches to the middle
nodes.definition: Natural dynamic systems can acquire formal participation through maintained complex state, while formally constructed systems can acquire dynamic attractor-like behavior through execution and learned inscription.

nodes.label: Token as path-writing event
nodes.definition: A token event selects a continuation, extends realized history, and becomes part of the conditions generating the next continuation field.

nodes.label: State-persistence speciation
nodes.definition: Passive, inscribed, active, recursive, plastic, and reconstructive persistence are distinct continuity mechanisms and must not be collapsed into one undifferentiated memory concept.

nodes.label: Formal–inscribed–executing boundary
nodes.definition: Formal structure, physical inscription, and executing process are distinct objects; preserving one does not automatically preserve the others.

nodes.label: Future-cone contraction
nodes.definition: For a uniform binary continuation tree, each admitted token halves the remaining measure of compatible infinite paths while leaving infinitely many paths after every finite prefix.

nodes.label: Reinstantiation is not resumption
nodes.definition: Recreating an executing process from durable inscription or a checkpoint is not identical to continuing the original active process unless the relevant execution state is preserved.

nodes.label: Object–process continuity
nodes.definition: Object-like and process-like organization differ by persistence mechanism, openness, and timescale rather than forming an absolute ontological boundary.

nodes.label: Qualified determinism
nodes.definition: Unique-successor determinism, distributional specification, exact-path determinism, and operational reproducibility are distinct claims and must be indexed to the declared state description.

nodes.label: Totality
nodes.definition: The single physically continuous causal system comprising all physically instantiated entities, processes, relations, and histories.

nodes.label: Analytic system cut
nodes.definition: A scale- and purpose-relative individuation of a region within Totality for description, measurement, or intervention.

nodes.label: Effective boundary
nodes.definition: A physically consequential or analytically selected distinction that separates a local system from its relative environment without severing causal continuity.

nodes.label: Totality regularity
nodes.definition: A persistent relational pattern or constraint in Totality that shapes repeated causal outcomes across locations, carriers, or scales.

nodes.label: Causal coherence
nodes.definition: Preservation of a relational feature across multiple causal outcomes, allowing different traces to remain jointly grounded in the same regularity.

nodes.label: Causal trace
nodes.definition: A downstream state difference that preserves one or more features of an originating event or regularity.

nodes.label: Trace carrier
nodes.definition: A physical system or inscribed structure in which a causal trace is instantiated, maintained, or propagated.

nodes.label: Trace transformation
nodes.definition: A causal transition that moves or recodes a trace between carriers while selectively preserving, modifying, or losing features.

nodes.label: Feature preservation
nodes.definition: The relation by which a trace or transformation retains a discriminable feature of an originating regularity.

nodes.label: Causal lineage
nodes.definition: An ordered chain of couplings and trace transformations connecting an originating regularity to a later inscription or response.

nodes.label: Inscription
nodes.definition: A persistent change in receiver organization that was caused by prior coupling and alters later transition tendencies.

nodes.label: Direct inscription
nodes.definition: Inscription produced through coupling between a receiver and the originating regularity without a representational relay.

nodes.label: Adaptive inscription
nodes.definition: Inscription retained or elaborated because it supports viable interaction with a persistent regularity.

nodes.label: Relayed inscription
nodes.definition: Inscription produced through causal traces transformed and carried by one or more intermediate systems.

nodes.label: Aggregated inscription
nodes.definition: Inscription produced by the convergent effect of many traces that preserve overlapping features of an originating regularity.

nodes.label: Representation
nodes.definition: An inscribed trace carrier organized to preserve selected features or relations of another event, system, or regularity.

nodes.label: Measurement
nodes.definition: A constrained coupling procedure that produces a trace intended to preserve a selected feature of a target.

nodes.label: Cross-carrier convergence
nodes.definition: Convergence of traces carried in different media or generated by different routes upon the same reconstructible region or distinction.

nodes.label: World-grounded learned region
nodes.definition: A reconstructible region in a learned transition landscape produced by direct or relayed inscriptions that preserve features of Totality.

nodes.label: Causal inheritance
nodes.definition: Transmission of constraint-shaped distinctions across a lineage of carriers, receivers, and inscriptions.

nodes.label: Semantic feature
nodes.definition: A named discriminable property or relation used by the ontology to communicate a recurring structure of Totality.

nodes.label: Semantic feature set
nodes.definition: The extensible graph of semantic features and typed relations through which this ontology describes Totality.

nodes.label: One-System principle
nodes.definition: There is one physically continuous causal system, Totality; all physically instantiated local systems are regions within it.

nodes.label: Individuation without separation
nodes.definition: Local systems are individuated by effective boundaries and analytic cuts, but remain causally continuous with Totality.

nodes.label: World-grounded inscription
nodes.definition: Persistent regularities in Totality shape receiver transition structures through direct coupling or through causally descended traces.

nodes.label: Relayed grounding
nodes.definition: A receiver may acquire a real distinction without direct encounter when a causal lineage preserves relevant features of the originating regularity.

nodes.label: Coherent-trace convergence
nodes.definition: Many heterogeneous traces that preserve overlapping features may reinforce one reconstructible region in a learned transition landscape.

nodes.label: Causally inherited region realism
nodes.definition: A learned region is operationally real when it descends from actual causal traces, is reconstructible across carriers or prompts, and changes future transitions.

nodes.label: Semantic-feature purpose
nodes.definition: The ontology is a graph for communicating a selected semantic feature set of Totality; it is not identical to Totality or an exhaustive copy of it.
